svg.aria-label: A KV session file as a byte map. The file is 101,057,232 bytes for this model at a 4096-token context: a 36-byte header, 24 layer records of 4,194,316 bytes each carrying K and V rows, 393,600 bytes of arena bookkeeping including one 16,384-byte owner table per layer, a length-prefixed host state blob, and a trailing 8-byte FNV-1a checksum. 99.6 percent of the file is KV rows.
svg.text: A KV SESSION AS A FILE: 101,057,232 BYTES
one model, 24 layers, 4,096 tokens, f32 cells - the layout `create` and `finish` write, in their order
24 layer records: 4,194,316 B each = 100,663,584 B (99.6 per cent)
arena bookkeeping 393,600 B (0.4 per cent) - drawn 6 px wide, not to scale
bytes 0-8 - magic "MINFERKV" - refused unless it is exactly this
bytes 8-12 - version 2 today; a reader refuses anything else, and version 2 added the host blob
bytes 12-16 - flags: bit 0 packed q8_0, bit 1 f16; every other bit is refused, which is why a new
element type did not need a version bump
bytes 16-36 - backend tag, n_layer, n_ctx, n_embd, row_elems - the geometry a load must match
then - 24 layer records of 4,194,316 B: index, k.len, v.len, then K words and V words
then - arena bookkeeping, the caller's host blob, and the FNV-1a checksum over all of it
the owner table is the surprising part: 4,096 u32 = 16,384 B per layer, so a restore knows which sequence holds each cell
every byte above the layer records is inside one FNV-1a checksum, which is why a one-byte corruption is refused instead of applied
